<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 450" width="700" height="450">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white" />

  <defs>
    <!-- Arrow marker for vectors -->
    <marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="5" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 1.5 L 10 5 L 0 8.5 z" fill="black" />
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- Styles -->
  <style>
    text {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 18px;
    }
    .label-std {
      font-style: normal;
    }
    .line {
      stroke: black;
      stroke-width: 1.5;
      fill: none;
    }
    .vector-label {
      font-weight: bold;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- Coordinates for Parallelogram ABCD and related points:
       B: (150, 320)
       C: (280, 100)
       D: (530, 100)
       A: (400, 320)
       
       Let's check parallelogram vectors:
       AD = D - A = (530-400, 100-320) = (130, -220)
       BC = C - B = (280-150, 100-320) = (130, -220)  -> Correct.
       
       CD = D - C = (530-280, 100-100) = (250, 0)
       CD : CE = 1 : 2 => CE = 2 * CD = 500 units right from C.
       E = C + (500, 0) = (280 + 500, 100) = (780, 100) -> Wait, viewport is 700 width!
       Let's scale down horizontally to fit 700 width.
       
       New coordinates:
       B: (120, 320)
       C: (250, 100)
       D: (450, 100)   [CD = 200]
       A: (320, 320)   [AB = (200, 0), AD = (130, -220)] -> Let's make AD vertical or slanted properly.
       
       Let's re-align:
       Parallelogram ABCD:
       B on left, C at top, D on right, A at bottom.
       B: (120, 300)
       C: (280, 100)
       D: (500, 100)   (CD = 220 vector b pointing right? Wait, CD goes from C to D. C=(280,100), D=(500,100). CD is horizontal, length 220.)
       A: (340, 300)   (AB is vector from B to A: (340-120, 300-300) = (220,0)? No, CD = AB for parallelogram ABCD. If CD is from C to D, then AB is from A to B or B to A? Standard order ABCD: AB, BC, CD, DA. So AB = CD. Here C=(280,100), D=(500,100). CD = (220, 0).
       Let's place vertices carefully:
       B: (120, 300)
       C: (240, 100)
       D: (440, 100)   (CD vector = 200 units right)
       A: (320, 300)   (AB vector = (200,0) from A to B? Wait. A to B is (-200, 0). Let's trace perimeter: A -> B -> C -> D -> A.
       A = (320, 300)
       B = (120, 300)  (AB = (-200, 0))
       C = (240, 100)  (BC = (120, -200))
       D = (440, 100)  (CD = (200, 0))
       DA = (320-440, 300-100) = (-120, 200), matches -BC. Perfect!
       
       Let's check CD and CE:
       CD = vector from C(240,100) to D(440,100). Length = 200.
       CD : CE = 1 : 2 => CE = 400.
       E lies on CD produced, so E = C + (400, 0) = (640, 100). This fits well within width 700!
       
       M is midpoint of AD:
       A = (320, 300), D = (440, 100)
       M = ((320+440)/2, (300+100)/2) = (380, 200).
       
       N is a point on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
       B = (120, 300), C = (240, 100)
       BC vector = (120, -200)
        BN = 1/4 BC = (30, -50)
       N = B + BN = (120 + 30, 300 - 50) = (150, 250).
       
       Vector a along BN:
       BN goes from B(120,300) to N(150,250).
       Vector b along CD:
       CD goes from C(240,100) to D(440,100).
       
       Lines to draw:
       - Parallelogram ABCD: polygon A-B-C-D (A(320,300), B(120,300), C(240,100), D(440,100))
       - Line CD produced to E: line from C through D to E(640,100).
       - Line ND: from N(150,250) to D(440,100).
       - Line BM: from B(120,300) to M(380,200).
       
       Wait, let's re-verify the prompt's layout description:
       "Parallelogram ABCD with B on the left, C at the top, D on the right and A at the bottom."
       My coordinates:
       B: (120, 300) - left
       C: (240, 100) - top
       D: (440, 100) - right (relative to C, but A is at (320, 300), so D is right of A and C).
       Wait, let's check standard parallelogram orientation where AB is bottom, CD is top:
       If AB is bottom, A is bottom-left, B is bottom-right?
       Prompt says: "B on the left, C at the top, D on the right and A at the bottom."
       Let's check my positions:
       B = (120, 300) [left]
       A = (320, 300) [bottom, right of B]
       C = (240, 100) [top, left of D]
       D = (440, 100) [right, top]
       Let's check connections:
       AB: (120,300) to (320,300) -> horizontal bottom edge.
       BC: (120,300) to (240,100) -> left slanted edge.
       CD: (240,100) to (440,100) -> horizontal top edge.
       DA: (440,100) to (320,300) -> right slanted edge.
       This is a valid parallelogram!
       B is on left, C is at top, D is on right, A is at bottom. Perfect.
       
       Let's re-check M (midpoint of AD):
       A(320,300), D(440,100).
       M = (380, 200). Lies on DA.
       
       Let's re-check N (on BC, BN:BC = 1:4):
       B(120,300), C(240,100).
       N = (150, 250). Lies on BC.
       
       Let's re-check E (CD produced, CD:CE = 1:2):
       C(240,100), D(440,100). CD = 200.
       CE = 400 from C. E = (640, 100).
       
       Lines required:
       - Parallelogram ABCD
       - CD extended to E (Segment C to E, with D on it)
       - Line ND
       - Line BM
       
       Vectors:
       - BN has vector a with arrow in the middle.
       - CD has vector b with arrow in the middle.
-->

  <!-- Lines of the parallelogram and extensions -->
  <!-- CE extension line -->
  <line x1="240" y1="100" x2="640" y2="100" class="line" />
  
  <!-- Other sides of parallelogram: AB, BC, DA -->
  <line x1="320" y1="300" x2="120" y2="300" class="line" /> <!-- AB -->
  <line x1="120" y1="300" x2="240" y2="100" class="line" /> <!-- BC -->
  <line x1="440" y1="100" x2="320" y2="300" class="line" /> <!-- DA -->

  <!-- Additional lines: ND and BM -->
  <line x1="150" y1="250" x2="440" y2="100" class="line" /> <!-- ND -->
  <line x1="120" y1="300" x2="380" y2="200" class="line" /> <!-- BM -->

  <!-- Vector a on BN (from B(120,300) to N(150,250)) -->
  <!-- Midpoint of BN is (135, 275) -->
  <line x1="120" y1="300" x2="150" y2="250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5" marker-middle="url(#arrow)" fill="none" />
  <!-- Since standard markers are at start/end, let's draw an explicit arrow or use a separate small line with marker for middle -->
  <line x1="131.5" y1="279" x2="138.5" y2="267" marker-end="url(#arrow)" stroke="none" />
  <!-- Actually, simpler and 100% reliable: draw vector arrow manually or use precise path with marker-end at midpoint -->
  <!-- Let's draw BN in two segments with an arrow head between them -->
  <!-- Vector a segment 1: (120,300) to (133, 278) -->
  <!-- Arrow at (135, 275) pointing towards (150, 250) -->
  <polygon points="139,268 131,273 134,277" fill="black" />
  <text x="110" y="275" class="vector-label">a</text>

  <!-- Vector b on CD (from C(240,100) to D(440,100)) -->
  <!-- Midpoint is (340, 100) -->
  <polygon points="345,95 355,100 345,105" fill="black" />
  <text x="335" y="85" class="vector-label">b</text>

  <!-- Vertex Labels -->
  <text x="100" y="325">B</text>
  <text x="225" y="90">C</text>
  <text x="445" y="90">D</text>
  <text x="315" y="325">A</text>
  <text x="645" y="105">E</text>
  <text x="130" y="245">N</text>
  <text x="390" y="200">M</text>

</svg>
